title: W4 fix broken: 'chronological' timeline sort compares mixed timestamp formats, so a same-day form-open renders ABOVE the earlier invitation/reminder line
description: view_attempt_summary sorts the timeline `lines` with `list.sort(fn(a, b) { string.compare(a.at, b.at) })` on the RAW `at` values, then claims in the comment: 'All `at` values are UTC ISO strings (RFC3339 from the sweep, PG `::text` for form_opened_at) — lexical sort is chronological.' That claim is false across the two formats. Attempts arrive RFC3339 with a 'T' separator ('2026-08-01T09:00:00Z'); form_opened_at arrives PG `::text` with a SPACE ('2026-08-01 14:00:00+00') — the very reason normalize_datetime (patch line 1138) exists, and it is applied ONLY to the `<time datetime>` attribute, not to the sort key. Byte-wise compare: on the same calendar date, position 10 is ' ' (0x20) vs 'T' (0x54); the space wins before any time digits are compared, so a form opened LATER the same day (e.g. 14:00) sorts ABOVE an invitation sent EARLIER (09:00) — verified byte-for-byte. The mini timeline renders 'Form opened 14:00' above 'Invitation sent 09:00' — chronologically reversed, in exactly the scenario the W4 fix (r1: 'form can open after a reminder... pinned-after-invite placement was wrong') claims to address. Fix: sort on normalize_datetime(line.at) (or normalize form_opened_at before inserting).
suggestion: Sort with string.compare(normalize_datetime(a.at), normalize_datetime(b.at)) so both formats compare on the RFC3339 form; add a test with a same-day later form_opened_at asserting the invitation/reminder line renders first.

title: W1 fix incomplete: em-dashes reintroduced as render-time literals in the mini timeline — the const-scan test cannot see them
description: The r1 fix removed em-dashes from the copy.gleam consts (refcheck_unmoderated_flag, refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed are clean) and the no_em_dash test was 'extended to scan refcheck consts'. But the timeline lines are assembled in reference_panel.gleam from string literals the const scan never sees: batch_line builds `TimelineLine(label <> " — " <> channels, at)` (patch line 1165) and nudge_label builds `copy.refcheck_timeline_nudge_skipped <> " — " <> skipped.detail` (patch line 1174). Rendered user-facing copy therefore still ships em-dashes — 'Invitation sent — email + SMS', 'Reminder 1 sent — email', 'Applicant nudge skipped — {detail}'. Timeline labels are implementer-authored (§7.6/§4.3 step labels; the diff's own spec lists them as implementer territory), so per the RT CI em-dash ban these are defects, and the 'fix' merely moved the dash out of const scope where the test can't catch it.
suggestion: Move the separator and the nudge-skipped join into copy.gleam consts without em-dashes (e.g. ' — ' → ', ' or ' · '), or extend the no_em_dash scan to cover string literals in the view module / rendered output.

title: 'Next reminder' line diverges from the diff's own spec quote: missing trailing period, and batches<3 vs shipped batches<4
description: The spec section of this very diff quotes the what-happens-next line with a trailing period and a cutoff: '"Next reminder in ~2 days if there's no reply." (verbatim §7.4) while a reminder is still pending (attempt batches < 3)'. The shipped copy const (copy.gleam, patch line 2000) is 'Next reminder in ~2 days if there's no reply' — no trailing period — and the code gates on `list.length(batches) < 4` (patch line 1085), not < 3. The < 4 cutoff does match the stated intent ('no line after the final reminder', with 2 reminders = 4 batches per the §7.4 cadence), so the spec parenthetical looks like the miscount — but the discrepancy is unexplained, and if the UX §7.4 source truly ends the sentence with a period (as the spec quote asserts), the shipped copy deviates from a verbatim line.
suggestion: Reconcile: add the trailing period if §7.4 has it, and correct the spec's '(attempt batches < 3)' parenthetical to '< 4' so the artifact matches the code.

title: W6 fix landed but inert: refcheck_explainer_dismissed is persisted + hydrated but never consumed by any view or handler
description: The §7.3 per-user explainer dismissal is written to localStorage on collapse (save_refcheck_explainer_dismissed_effect), hydrated at boot (hydrate_refcheck_explainer_dismissed_effect), and threaded through the model — but nothing ever READS it. The panel's view() takes only `explainer_open`; application_detail passes only `explainer_open: model.refcheck_explainer_open`; route-change resets `refcheck_explainer_open` to False unconditionally. The explainer is collapsed by default regardless of the dismissed flag, so the persisted state has zero observable effect — the W6 'fix' is write-only plumbing. Dead state that will confuse future maintainers (it looks like it gates first-visit display).
suggestion: Either consume the flag (e.g. suppress a first-visit open-state, or drive the initial open state from it) or remove the persistence + hydration entirely — the collapsed-by-default behavior alone satisfies the spec.

title: Stale duplicated doc comment on answered_count — leftover from the r1 rework
description: answered_count carries TWO stacked doc comments (patch lines 1419-1428). The first block ('Mirrors the structurer's completeness notion: a field is answered when its verification value is a non-null string or object; the free-text array counts only when non-empty.') describes the pre-rework semantics; the second block ('The count mirrors the RENDERER exactly ... so a content-less object can never inflate m (rc4-2 Perkins r1 N7)') supersedes it with the renderer-mirror semantics the code actually implements (it counts via render_value != 'Not answered'). The first comment is a stale duplicate from the fix that changed the counting semantics — a textbook rework leftover.
suggestion: Delete the first (structurer-completeness) doc block; keep only the renderer-mirror explanation.

title: worth_knowing_signals comment overclaims: 'flags' rows 'map here too' but no flags field is ever decoded
description: The doc comment on worth_knowing_signals (patch lines 1631-1633) states 'The `flags`/`geo` rows of the §7.5 table that v1 never emits (no flags field; geo is always "unknown") map here too, so a future payload fires them honestly.' Only geo maps: signals_decoder decodes geo_vs_claimed_property (and form_session plus five booleans) — there is no `flags` key anywhere in the decoder. A future payload carrying flags would have them silently dropped, contradicting the comment's claim that they fire honestly. Comment claims behavior the code doesn't have.
suggestion: Either decode a `flags` list into the Signals type and render its entries, or amend the comment to say only geo maps (flags are not yet surfaced).
